claim: Team datathon used 215,440 website records after cleaning 228,178 raw rows.
caveat: No multi-agent conversations or real click behavior.

claim: Reported data split: 91,945 phishing websites and 123,495 legitimate sites.
caveat: Case-control ratio is not population prevalence.

claim: Reported logistic classifier: 95.8 percent accuracy and 95.0 percent phishing recall under five-fold domain-grouped CV.
caveat: Not production performance; legitimate URLs sampling biased.

claim: Reported 49.1 percent of phishing websites used HTTPS.
The datathon dataset included no observed user messages or clicks.

caveat: Complaints are not confirmed independent incidents or agent-related cases.

claim: FBI IC3 2025 reported about 3.05 billion USD in business email compromise losses and about 8.65 billion USD in investment fraud losses.
caveat: Categories differ; do not call these PhishNet-addressable losses.

claim: SCAMBENCH contains 1,836 scam and 1,834 non-scam messages with evidence-grounded annotation.
caveat: CC BY-NC 4.0 gated dataset; not acquired here.

claim: Five LLM-based detectors performed worse on scam examples reworded to remove obvious cues.
caveat: No quoted performance delta; refer to paper for methods.

claim: Bank of England FCA 2026 survey reported 80 percent full-survey agent deployment and only 2 percent broad autonomy.
caveat: Sampling and denominator matter; percentages overlap by autonomy.

claim: No more than 9 percent of surveyed respondents planned/current agents for sensitive tasks including payments in next 12 months.
caveat: Cannot extrapolate to all global financial firms.

claim: Visa Onchain Analytics observed 298.9 million x402+MPP transactions and 58.6 million USD unadjusted tracked volume at snapshot.
caveat: Dynamic snapshot; not verified autonomous or revenue.

claim: Visa Onchain Analytics reported 34.8 million USD adjusted organic volume and approximately 0.009997 USD median transaction.
caveat: Organic is an estimate, not ground truth of real customers.

claim: A verified cryptographic signature proves key control over a signed message, not truthfulness of its claim.
caveat: Signatures need recipient/chain/amount/expiry/nonce binding and trusted identity records.

claim: Merkle inclusion proofs show an event commitment belongs to a root; they do not prove all events were collected.
caveat: Preserve privacy and chain of custody.

claim: Never permit language model risk judgments to override deterministic authorization policy.
caveat: Must be tested at tool and signer boundary.

claim: If an agent says verified but only copies a single unverified source, the claim remains unverified.
caveat: Source multiplication is not independent evidence.

claim: Consumer advisory mode does not claim control of external payments it cannot enforce.
caveat: Keep advisor and SaaS enforcement separate.

claim: A new vendor recipient with independent authenticated verification and fresh signed intent can be legitimate.
